# One decision tree per input, generated by a light Generator

The Generator builds a separate decision tree for every input, and that tree is saved once and reused across every condition. The alternative was one tree per task, built from the root decision alone without seeing any input. We chose per-input trees because they adapt to each input, which is how the method would be used in practice.

## Consequences

Because the Generator reads the input, it could leak the answer into its sub-decisions, and any improvement could then come from the Generator instead of the tree. To guard against this, the Generator is deliberately a light model, it is told never to state or hint at the answer to a parent, a sample of trees is checked by hand, and the paper reports a Generator-only baseline where the Generator answers the root decision directly. One tree per task stays available as an optional ablation.
